items.title: Weighted-draw movement for the Dead with aggregates and company pull

notes.text: D-007 (see decisions.md) fixes the shape of the draw: weight a candidate cell by pow(scent, k) with a tunable exponent k slightly above 1, never exp(k*scent) — at the 0-500 scale from PEO-026 exp saturates immediately. A power law keys off the ratio between neighbouring cells, so one k stays decisive next to the player and becomes a gentle drift far away, which is the horde-drift behaviour the user asked for. Fold this into the brief when PEO-009 is planned.

PEO-007 constraint: World::commit re-decides only the Dead within 2 cells of the player, so a Dead's decision must not depend on how many others decided before it. The weighted draw must take its randomness from a counter-based hash of (world seed, stage, turn, Dead index), never from one shared Rng stream consumed in horde order, or commit(speculate()) stops being bit-identical to step(). Keep the golden test in test_world.cpp passing.

D-022 (N016) settles Dead speed: probabilistic extra steps per update, built in PEO-042 ahead of this item. The pathfinding review found that occupancy and a wake-up cascade make moves order-dependent, which breaks the commit patch; the draw needs an intents-then-resolve step, and PEO-022 stacks on that.

notes.text: D-010 (2026-09-29): the far layer becomes a buildup layer. A cell's fade rate falls as the sliding 3x3 box total around it rises, to a nonzero minimum; box totals refresh on a turn schedule (every turn near the player, staggered further out); buildup pulls harder than a fresh trail. The separable IIR solve assumes a single decay everywhere, so re-examine the method (e.g. a coarse FTCS far layer stepped on a stagger) when briefing. Acceptance adds: a den where the player lingered, and a path walked often, both outlast and outpull a fresh trail.

PEO-007 constraint: compute D-010 fade rates (box totals) at the start of a turn from committed state, before the player's deposit is patched in, so speculate() sees the same rates commit() uses; the golden test must stay bit-exact. If a rate had to depend on this turn's deposit, commit would need to recompute every cell whose box includes the patched cells.

D-013 (2026-09-29) supersedes D-010's fade rule: buildup moves to a per-tile soak value (PEO-038), so the far layer returns to a single decay and D-008's separable IIR solve stands. Drop the buildup acceptance from this item; the doorway scenario stays.

Waits on D-024 (transport). The pathfinding review (reviews/2026-09-29-pathfinding-and-scent-review.md) measured the IIR far layer failing on a town map; D-019 and D-020 (N016) add reach radius, wind and indoor rules the transport must carry. Rebrief once D-024 is answered.
D-024 answered: A. Rebriefed as the geodesic field; D-008's two layers and the IIR far layer are superseded. Build after PEO-035.

items.title: Soak: a capped per-tile scent memory charged by contact (D-013)

notes.text: Walls: Ryan asked whether keeping 10% of wall-bound scent would help buildup. Probe: a 10% bounce raises indoor values only 2-10% (camp tile 1110 to 1130), and soak is fed by contact, not the field, so walls stay fully absorbing.
D-015: soak charges and leaks per game second, so it runs on the one-second world clock (PEO-040).

D-028 answered: B. Portable absorbers (mattress, cushion, clothing) carry soak as a value on the thing and take it with them; floors and fixed furniture keep it on the tile. D-024: the field is integer log strength, so express soak in the same units and have the Dead read the larger of field and soak (a log-sum approximation); PEO-055 derives the per-object soak rate.

items.title: Rot: section counts of the Dead mask human scent (D-012)

notes.text: D-025 (open) asks whether rot masks by scaling instead of 1:1 subtraction; the pathfinding review measured subtraction zeroing every cell past about 12 cells. Fold the answer into the draw formula before starting. PEO-051 may supply the section grid.

D-025 answered: A. In the geodesic field (D-024, PEO-030) values are log strength, so a Dead subtracts rot x a named scale from the value it reads; it dulls the pull and never zeroes a distant trail. Replaces D-012's 1:1 subtraction. Build on ScentWave, after PEO-030.
